evals.prompt: The claude-pr-review bot just posted a FAIL on my open PR. It flagged exactly two Must-fix items: (1) a missing `.js` extension on the relative import on line 2 of `packages/m3l-common/src/core/config/index.ts`, and (2) a bare string throw `throw 'not found'` on line 7 of the same file. No Should-fix or Nits were listed. Fix both findings, run the required quality gates, commit, push, and post a follow-up comment on the PR.
evals.expected_output: The skill prints a two-item Must-fix preview, reads the seeded source file, applies both fixes (corrected import path and M3LError subclass throw), emits WOULD-RUN lines for pnpm typecheck after the ESM fix and pnpm lint after the error-handling fix, emits the final full-gate WOULD-RUN, then states it will commit and post a top-level PR comment with the commit SHA.
expectations: Prints a preview listing exactly two Must-fix findings — the extensionless import and the bare string throw — before describing any file edits.
Reads the seeded `packages/m3l-common/src/core/config/index.ts` and the response includes the literal string `./types.js` showing the corrected import path.
Emits a `WOULD-RUN: pnpm typecheck` line after describing the `.js`-extension fix and before describing the error-handling fix.
Emits a `WOULD-RUN: pnpm lint` line after describing the replacement of the bare string throw.
Emits a `WOULD-RUN: pnpm verify` line for the final full-gate check before the commit step.
States it will post a top-level PR comment referencing the commit SHA, and names that step after the push step.

evals.prompt: I just opened a PR and the claude-pr-review bot reviewed it. The comment shows a PASS verdict, an empty Must-fix section, one Should-fix item (missing `@example` on `loadConfig` in `packages/m3l-common/src/core/config/index.ts`), and one Nit (prefer `const` over `let` on line 4 of the same file). Run resolving-pr-comments to confirm there is nothing to do.
evals.expected_output: The skill names fetching the bot comment as its first substantive step, detects the PASS verdict, still prints the Should-fix and Nit items for context (Must-fix omitted as empty), and stops without editing, committing, or pushing anything.
expectations: Names fetching the claude[bot] comment from the PR thread as its first substantive step (states the intent to retrieve or read the bot comment before any other action).
Identifies the PASS verdict and explicitly states nothing is blocking, using language such as 'already shows PASS' or 'nothing blocking'.
Prints the Should-fix item (missing `@example` on `loadConfig`) and the Nit item (prefer `const` over `let`) for context, rather than silently dropping them because the verdict is PASS.
Emits no `WOULD-RUN: git commit` or `WOULD-RUN: git push` line anywhere in the response.
Does not describe any file edits and does not list any Must-fix findings to resolve.

evals.prompt: There's an open PR on this branch. The only comment on the PR thread is from `github-actions[bot]`, posted just now. Its body begins with the line `## Claude PR Review — not run`, followed by prose stating the reviewable diff is 340,000 characters, over the 300,000-character limit for a single-pass review, lists the largest contributing files, and says to split the PR. No `claude[bot]` comment exists anywhere on the thread. Run resolving-pr-comments.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects the PR, fetches the comment thread, recognizes the sole comment as the oversize-rejection path (body starts with `## Claude PR Review — not run`, posted by github-actions[bot] rather than claude[bot]) rather than a normal review, and stops immediately telling the user the PR was too large for a single-pass review and must be split — without attempting to parse or fix any Must-fix findings.
expectations: Names fetching the PR's comment thread as an early step, describing the intent to look for a bot review comment.
Explicitly identifies the sole comment as the oversize-rejection path — its body begins with `## Claude PR Review — not run` — rather than treating it as a completed claude[bot] review.
Tells the user the PR's reviewable diff was too large for a single-pass review and that no review ran, using language such as 'too large' or 'split the PR'.
References splitting the PR into smaller pieces (optionally citing `docs/contributing/branch-protection.md`) as the recommended next action.
Emits no `WOULD-RUN: git commit` or `WOULD-RUN: git push` line, and does not list or describe any Must-fix findings to fix.

evals.prompt: There's an open PR on this branch with a 150-comment thread, fetched in pages of 100. Page 1 (the first 100 comments, oldest first) ends with a `claude[bot]` review comment — call it comment A — showing a PASS verdict. Page 2 (comments 101-150) contains further human discussion and ends with a second `claude[bot]` review comment — call it comment B — which is the true most recent comment on the whole thread, showing a FAIL verdict with exactly one Must-fix item: a bare string throw `throw 'invalid input'` on line 9 of `packages/m3l-common/src/core/config/index.ts`. Fetch the full comment thread, act on the correct (most recent) verdict, fix the Must-fix item, run the required quality gates, commit, push, and post a follow-up comment.
evals.expected_output: The skill describes paging past the first 100-comment page to reach the second page, correctly identifies comment B (not the stale comment A) as the most recent bot comment, acts on its FAIL verdict, fixes the single Must-fix item, runs the gates, and proceeds to commit and post a follow-up comment — rather than stopping early on comment A's stale PASS.
expectations: Describes paging past the first 100-comment page to retrieve the second page, rather than stopping after the first page's results.
Acts on comment B's FAIL verdict (the true most recent comment), not comment A's stale PASS — does not stop early claiming the review already shows PASS or that there is nothing to fix.
Prints a one-item Must-fix preview naming the bare string throw on line 9 of `packages/m3l-common/src/core/config/index.ts`.
Reads the seeded file and the response describes replacing the bare string throw with an `M3LError` subclass rather than a plain string throw.
Emits a `WOULD-RUN: pnpm lint` line after describing the fix, and a `WOULD-RUN: pnpm verify` line before the commit step.
States it will commit, push, and post a top-level PR comment referencing the commit SHA.

evals.prompt: The claude-pr-review bot posted a FAIL on my open PR against `packages/m3l-common/src/core/config/index.ts`. It flagged: one Must-fix (a missing `.js` extension on the relative import on line 2), one Should-fix (missing TSDoc/`@example` on `loadConfig`, line 6), and two Nits — Nit A: prefer double quotes over single quotes for the import path string literal on line 2 (the same line as the Must-fix), and Nit B: prefer `const` with a setter over the mutable `let cache` on line 4 (an unrelated line no other fix touches). Fix what should be fixed given this project's tiered fix policy, run the required quality gates, commit, push, and post a follow-up comment.
evals.expected_output: The skill prints a preview showing all four findings across their tiers, fixes the Must-fix import, fixes the Should-fix TSDoc gap, folds Nit A into the same edit as the Must-fix (since it shares line 2), leaves Nit B untouched (since line 4 is never otherwise edited), then runs gates, commits with tier-separated bullets, and posts a follow-up comment listing Must-fix/Should-fix resolved, Nit A folded in, and Nit B as not addressed.
expectations: Prints a preview listing all four findings (the Must-fix, the Should-fix, and both Nits) across their correct tiers before describing any file edits.

Reads the seeded file and the response includes the literal string `./types.js` showing the corrected, double-quoted import path — resolving the Must-fix and folding in Nit A (the quote-style Nit) in the same edit, since both touch line 2.
The response describes adding a TSDoc block with `@example` to `loadConfig`, resolving the Should-fix item.
Explicitly states or implies that the `let cache` declaration on line 4 (Nit B) is left untouched, since no Must-fix or Should-fix edit in this pass touches that line.
Emits a `WOULD-RUN: pnpm typecheck` line covering the ESM-imports-category fixes, and a `WOULD-RUN: pnpm verify` line before the commit step.
Describes the commit body as separating Must-fix, Should-fix, and folded-in-Nits into distinct groups rather than one flat list.
States the follow-up comment will list the Must-fix and Should-fix items resolved, Nit A as folded in, and Nit B under Not addressed.
